hypothesis: Most residual error of the routed 10 m LWC84 Marmousi backbone is representable by one causal global travel-time warp, so an oracle scale on a fixed grid can reduce every sampled train record to at most 5 percent relative L2.
purpose: Cheap capacity rejection test before training any phase-warp adapter. Oracle truth-dependent choices are diagnostic upper bounds and are prohibited at deployment.

data_contract.selection: Six stable f0 quantiles after excluding every medium group in all three DRP experiments.

probe_contract.physical_backbone_route: Taylor-8 below 24 Hz; DRP-0.45 at or above 24 Hz.
probe_contract.warp_definition: p_warp(t,x,z)=p_backbone(t+s*T(x,z),x,z), with linear interpolation and zero outside the stored time interval.
reported_bounds: best per-record warp plus oracle scalar amplitude
probe_contract.capacity_pass_rule: All six best fixed-amplitude oracle errors are <= 0.05. The amplitude oracle is reported only to distinguish phase versus amplitude capacity.
probe_contract.failure_signal: Any fixed-amplitude oracle record exceeds 0.05, any sample/cache digest differs, or any non-train record is read.
probe_contract.rollback: Reject one-scalar travel-time warping and move to a multiscale learned residual closure conditioned on the physical backbone.

test_evidence.coverage: warp identity, half-step interpolation and zero-outside semantics plus fused solver regression tests

prohibited_uses: Oracle scale and amplitude may never be used as online adaptation inputs.
No validation or test_id wavefield may be read.
No 5 percent or 10x claim may be made from this train-only capacity probe.
